project.name: hypermnesia-mcp
project.description: Cortex is a local-first persistent memory MCP server for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop), implementing a scientifically-grounded memory system based on computational neuroscience research, backed by SQLite or PostgreSQL + pgvector. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.languageNotes: Loads a historical version of a module via `git show` and `exec` into a namespace to benchmark old vs. new code side by side.

nodes.summary: Core ``chronic_interference`` lands every SIGNAL_POOL row in its band.

nodes.summary: Checks that background neighbours leave chronic interference at zero while a single exact duplicate drives it up.

nodes.name: series_reproduced
nodes.summary: Baked (λ, Θ_accum) reproduce every S1–S5 fire/never/recovery label.

nodes.name: transient_reproduced
nodes.summary: Verifies that the transient-forgetting circuit reproduces every labelled transient fixture row.

nodes.name: fixture_consolidated_graded_not_immune
nodes.summary: Checks that consolidated memories resist but are not immune to permanent forgetting under sustained strong chronic interference.

nodes.name: fixture_sleep_protects_permanent
nodes.summary: Sustained chronic but sleep-protected EVERY cycle ⇒ never permanent (sleep zeroes pressure and the accumulator leaks; Davis&Zhong).

nodes.name: fixture_zero_chronic_no_permanent
nodes.summary: No chronic driver ⇒ accumulator stays 0 ⇒ no permanent, any stage.

nodes.name: fixture_transient_stage_independent
nodes.summary: An acute recent interferer triggers transient regardless of stage.

nodes.name: fixture_transient_needs_recency_and_overlap
nodes.summary: Transient requires BOTH overlap≥X AND age≤W (the AND, not either).

nodes.name: fixture_circuits_independent_no_conversion
nodes.summary: Check that transient and permanent forgetting circuits remain independent.

nodes.name: fixture_reversibility
nodes.summary: Both modes reversible. Transient recovers on re-access (recently_active). Permanent is reinstated: once interference abates, the accumulator leaks back below Θ (the S5 decay-recovery trajectory).

nodes.name: fixture_hippocampal_dependency_non_regression
nodes.summary: Check the permanent-forgetting trigger for zero hippocampal dependency.

nodes.name: fixture_hippocampal_dependency_protects
nodes.summary: Check that full hippocampal dependency reduces accumulated pressure.

nodes.name: fixture_hippocampal_dependency_never_zeroes_pressure
nodes.summary: Check that full hippocampal dependency leaves pressure strictly positive.

nodes.name: external_phases.py
nodes.summary: Attributes powermetrics power samples to the ingest/recall phase timeline written by retrieval benchmarks (LongMemEval, LoCoMo, BEAM), reporting whole-leg and per-condition energy and SCI carbon per query.

nodes.name: Window
nodes.summary: Dataclass for one timed benchmark phase window (condition, start, end) with an elapsed-seconds property.

nodes.name: load_windows
nodes.summary: Loads phase windows from a benchmark's .phases.jsonl timeline file.

nodes.name: leg_summary

depth.signature: leg_summary(samples: list[tuple[float, float]], windows: list[Window]) -> dict[str, float]

nodes.name: measurement.py
nodes.summary: Parses macOS powermetrics combined CPU+GPU+ANE power samples, applies them to measured phases, computes SCI carbon per 1k tokens, and writes reproducible energy report artifacts with manifests.

nodes.name: MeasuredPhase
nodes.summary: Dataclass for a benchmark phase with tokens, duration and mean power, deriving raw system and dynamic (idle-subtracted) energy.

depth.signature: parse_power_samples(text: str, phase_end: float | None) -> list[tuple[float, float]]

nodes.name: apply_power_samples

depth.signature: apply_power_samples(phases: list[Phase], samples: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> list[MeasuredPhase]

nodes.name: carbon_per_1k_tokens
nodes.summary: Computes SCI carbon (operational E/3.6e6*I plus embodied M) per thousand tokens, refusing invalid inputs.

depth.signature: carbon_per_1k_tokens(energy_j: float, tokens: int, intensity: float, embodied_g: float) -> float

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Summarizes measured phases into energy and carbon metrics using actual token counts and embodied-phase duration.

depth.signature: summarize(rows: list[MeasuredPhase], mode: str, args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, float]

nodes.name: change_remediation.py
nodes.summary: Pure core policy deciding how to remediate memories impacted by a code change: re-ingest code-derived memories, flag hand-authored ones as stale (ADR-0122).

nodes.name: Remediation
nodes.summary: String enum of remediation actions: REINGEST or FLAG_STALE.

nodes.name: is_code_derived
nodes.summary: Returns true when a memory came from codebase ingestion, via agent_context 'codebase' or a codebase/hash tag fallback.

nodes.name: classify_remediation
nodes.summary: REINGEST a code-derived memory; FLAG_STALE a hand-authored one.

nodes.name: change_remediation_pass.py
nodes.summary: Consolidation-pass composition root that applies the change-remediation policy to diff-impacted memories, batching deduplicated re-ingest paths and marking hand-authored memories stale via an injected store.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a typing.Protocol for the store and an injected callback so the pass unit-tests with fakes.

nodes.name: remediate_impacted
nodes.summary: Splits impacted memories into re-ingest (dedup'd changed refs passed to reingest_fn) and flag-stale (store.mark_memory_stale), returning counts.

depth.signature: remediate_impacted(impacted: list[dict], store: _RemediationStore, reingest_fn: ReingestFn) -> dict[str, int]

nodes.name: _RemediationStore
nodes.summary: Protocol describing the store capability needed by the pass: mark_memory_stale.

nodes.name: emergence_metrics.py

nodes.name: metacognition.py
nodes.summary: Pure core module for metacognitive gap detection: finds isolated entities, stale memory regions, low-confidence memories, missing entity connections and unresolved errors, then merges them into a severity-sorted gap list (backs the detect_gaps tool).

nodes.name: metacognition_analysis.py
nodes.summary: Pure core module for knowledge coverage scoring (density and recency), entity/temporal chunking of memories, primacy-recency context management, and overflow summarization that preserves high-surprise and high-importance memories.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ordered threshold tables of (timedelta, score) tuples for piecewise scoring instead of if-chains.

nodes.name: test_metacognition.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite covering coverage computation, every gap detector, combined gap ranking, memory chunking, context management and overflow summarization in the metacognition core modules.

nodes.name: detect_isolated_entities
nodes.summary: Flags entities with zero or one relationship as isolated-knowledge gaps with severity by degree.

depth.signature: detect_isolated_entities(entities: list[dict[str, Any]], relationship_counts: dict[int, int]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: detect_stale_regions
nodes.summary: Detects domains or directories whose memories have all gone stale, reporting them as stale-region gaps above a minimum count.

depth.signature: detect_stale_regions(memories: list[dict[str, Any]], heat_threshold: float, min_stale: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: detect_low_confidence
nodes.summary: Returns gaps for memories whose metamemory confidence falls below the threshold.

depth.signature: detect_low_confidence(memories: list[dict[str, Any]], confidence_threshold: float) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: detect_missing_connections
nodes.summary: Finds frequently co-occurring entity pairs that lack a relationship in either direction.

depth.signature: detect_missing_connections(co_occurring_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]], existing_relationships: set[tuple[str, str]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: detect_unresolved_errors
nodes.summary: Reports error memories that have no corresponding resolution memory.

depth.signature: detect_unresolved_errors(error_entities: list[dict[str, Any]], resolved_entity_ids: set[int]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: detect_all_gaps
nodes.summary: Runs every gap detector and returns the combined gaps sorted by descending severity.

depth.signature: detect_all_gaps(entities: list[dict[str, Any]], relationship_counts: dict[int, int], memories: list[dict[str, Any]], co_occurring_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]], existing_relationships: set[tuple[str, str]], error_entities: list[dict[str, Any]], resolved_entity_ids: set[int], heat_threshold: float, confidence_threshold: float) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: compute_coverage
nodes.summary: Computes a 0-1 coverage score for a query from match density and recency, classifying it as sufficient, partial or insufficient.

depth.signature: compute_coverage(matching_count: int, entity_coverage: float, newest_age: timedelta | None, avg_confidence: float, weights: tuple[float, float, float, float]) -> dict[str, Any]

nodes.name: _should_join_chunk
nodes.summary: Decides whether a memory joins the current chunk based on entity Jaccard overlap or temporal proximity.

depth.signature: _should_join_chunk(mem_i: dict, mem_j: dict, ents_i: set[str], time_i: datetime | None, entity_overlap_threshold: float, window: timedelta) -> bool

nodes.name: _collect_chunk
nodes.summary: Greedily gathers unassigned memories that should join a seed memory's chunk.

depth.signature: _collect_chunk(seed_idx: int, mem: dict, memories: list[dict[str, Any]], assigned: set[int], entity_overlap_threshold: float, window: timedelta) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: chunk_memories
nodes.summary: Groups memories into coherent chunks by shared entities and temporal proximity.

depth.signature: chunk_memories(memories: list[dict[str, Any]], entity_overlap_threshold: float, temporal_window_hours: float) -> list[list[dict[str, Any]]]

nodes.name: _position_selected_chunks
nodes.summary: Reorders selected chunks so the strongest sit at the start and end of context (primacy-recency).

depth.signature: _position_selected_chunks(selected: list[tuple[int, float, list[dict[str, Any]]]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: manage_context
nodes.summary: Scores and selects up to a max number of chunks for context, applies primacy-recency positioning and marks overflow.

depth.signature: manage_context(memories: list[dict[str, Any]], max_chunks: int | None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.summary: Condenses overflowed memories into a capped summary while keeping high-surprise and high-importance memories verbatim.

depth.signature: summarize_overflow(excess_memories: list[dict[str, Any]], target_count: int, surprise_threshold: float, importance_threshold: float) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context exclusions dropping VCS data, caches, virtualenvs, build artifacts, local agent state and generated benchmark outputs while keeping .claude/settings.json.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage production image for the Cortex MCP server: a builder stage installs the uv.lock-pinned dependency set (postgresql extra, CPU-only torch) and builds the project wheel, and a slim non-root runtime stage runs `python -m mcp_server` over stdio with SQLite by default and optional PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL.
nodes.languageNotes: Base images and the uv binary are pinned by sha256 digest, and dependencies are installed with `uv sync --locked` so the image is reproducible from the lockfile.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Build stage on python:3.14-slim that compiles native deps with gcc/libpq-dev, syncs the locked venv with uv and installs the built Cortex wheel without deps.

nodes.name: runtime
nodes.summary: Runtime stage copying the prebuilt venv, adding libpq5, running as uid 10001 with CORTEX_RUNTIME=cowork, an import healthcheck and the stdio MCP entrypoint.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: ClusterFuzzLite build environment on the digest-pinned OSS-Fuzz Python base-builder image; copies the repo and uv into $SRC and installs build.sh to compile the atheris/libFuzzer harnesses under fuzz/.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Dev container image on a pinned python:3.14-slim base that installs build tools and the PostgreSQL client, syncs dependencies from uv.lock, installs Cortex editable, pre-caches the embedding model under a persistent HF_HOME, and runs as a non-root cortex user.
nodes.languageNotes: Base image and the uv binary are pinned by sha256 digest; dependencies resolve from the locked uv.lock rather than pyproject ranges.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Dev container compose stack pairing the Cortex app container (built from the devcontainer Dockerfile, workspace bind-mounted, idling with sleep infinity) with a pgvector/pgvector:pg16 database that has a healthcheck, persistent volume and initdb scripts.

nodes.name: app
nodes.summary: Compose service that builds the devcontainer image, mounts the repo at /workspace, points DATABASE_URL/libpq env at the db service, and waits for db health.

nodes.name: db
nodes.summary: PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector compose service with dev-only credentials, named data volume, init scripts and pg_isready healthcheck.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage runtime image bundling the full Cortex memory system: a builder stage installs Node.js 22, the pinned Claude Code CLI, a uv.lock-resolved venv and pre-downloaded models; the final stage adds PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector, a non-root cortex user, persistent data volumes and an entrypoint that runs Claude Code with Cortex wired over stdio.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build copies only the venv, Node binary, Claude Code and Hugging Face cache from the builder, keeping compilers out of the runtime layer; base images are pinned by digest.

nodes.name: builder
nodes.summary: Builder stage that installs Node.js and Claude Code via npm ci, creates /opt/venv from uv.lock, installs Cortex editable and pre-downloads embedding/reranker models with retries.

nodes.name: runtime
nodes.summary: Final runtime stage installing PostgreSQL 17 + pgvector, copying builder artifacts, initializing the database cluster, and setting DATABASE_URL, CORTEX_MEMORY_STORE_BACKEND=postgresql and the entrypoint.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: Main CI pipeline on push/PR/weekly schedule: path filtering, Python test matrix, SQLite and Windows legs, MCP host config validation, ruff lint plus doc/version/badge checks, craftsmanship gate, pyright typecheck, package and Docker builds, bare-container smoke test, install end-to-end runs, an aggregated CI Green gate and a release-tag job.

nodes.name: fuzz.yml
nodes.summary: ClusterFuzzLite workflow that builds and runs coverage-guided fuzzers over the pure parsers in fuzz/, as a short batch on PRs and a longer weekly scheduled batch.

nodes.name: hol-plugin-scanner.yml
nodes.summary: Runs the HOL AI plugin scanner action against the repository on push, PR and a weekly Tuesday schedule to catch plugin-security rule drift.

nodes.name: marketplace-pins.yml
nodes.summary: Gate that runs check_marketplace_pins.py to ensure plugin marketplace pins match the latest releases, on relevant PR/push changes and weekly.

nodes.name: mcp-toplist-badge.yml
nodes.summary: Monthly workflow that refreshes the MCP Toplist rank badge via refresh_mcp_toplist_badge.py and opens a pull request with the update.

nodes.name: publish-ccplugins.yml
nodes.summary: On published releases (or manual dry-run dispatch) syncs the hypermnesia-mcp plugin bundle into a fork of awesome-claude-code-plugins and opens or updates an upstream pull request.

nodes.name: release.yml
nodes.summary: Tag-triggered release pipeline creating the GitHub Release, building and attesting sdist/wheel, generating a CycloneDX SBOM from uv.lock, packaging an attested MCPB bundle for Claude Desktop, and best-effort publishing to PyPI and the MCP registry.

nodes.name: scorecard.yml
nodes.summary: OpenSSF Scorecard supply-chain posture analysis on push, branch-protection changes and weekly, uploading SARIF results to code scanning.

nodes.name: sync-ccplugins-fork.yml
nodes.summary: Keeps the ccplugins fork's main branch fast-forwarded from upstream on pushes to main, daily, and on manual dispatch.

nodes.name: upstream-identity.yml
nodes.summary: Weekly and per-change conformance check that fetches the upstream codebase-intelligence identity contract and verifies the repo does not use revoked Claude tool prefixes.

nodes.name: .bestpractices.json

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Guide to reproducing Cortex benchmarks with one command (reproduce.sh), the scope of reported metrics, other benchmarks, and per-query journal/token/energy accounting.

nodes.name: repro_longmemeval.sh

nodes.languageNotes: `exec` replaces the shell process, so the function definitions after it never run.

nodes.name: reproduce.sh
nodes.summary: Release-gate benchmark harness: provisions an isolated ephemeral PostgreSQL container, fetches pinned datasets, runs LongMemEval/LoCoMo/BEAM (plus optional ablation sweeps), writes a provenance manifest, prints a summary and enforces score floors.

nodes.name: trust_factor_sweep.sh
nodes.summary: Resumable grid sweep over CORTEX_UNTRUSTED_ORIGIN_FACTOR values, running one pending cell of reproduce.sh per invocation with machine-load/disk snapshots and progress tracking.

nodes.name: fetch_dataset
nodes.summary: Downloads the LongMemEval dataset if missing and verifies its SHA-256 pin.

nodes.name: start_db
nodes.summary: Starts a fresh pgvector Docker container and waits until the database accepts connections, dumping logs on failure.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Checks prerequisites, fetches the dataset, starts the DB and runs the LongMemEval harness with teardown on exit.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Parses CLI flags such as --quick, --only, --no-ablation, --limit and ablation target into globals.

nodes.name: check_reranker_cell
nodes.summary: Verifies the reranker configuration cell before running so benchmarks are not silently invalidated.

nodes.name: fetch_longmemeval
nodes.summary: Fetches the pinned LongMemEval-S dataset and verifies its checksum.

nodes.name: fetch_longmemeval_cleaned
nodes.summary: Fetches the pinned cleaned LongMemEval-S variant and verifies its checksum.

nodes.name: acquire_lock
nodes.summary: Takes a directory lock so only one reproduce run uses the benchmark container at a time.

nodes.name: run_bench
nodes.summary: Runs one run_benchmark.py harness against the ephemeral DB and captures its output into the results directory.

nodes.name: run_ablation_sweep
nodes.summary: Invokes the ablation runner to lesion mechanisms one at a time for the selected benchmark.

nodes.name: print_summary
nodes.summary: Prints a summary table of benchmark scores (and ablation deltas) from the results artifacts via an inline Python block.

nodes.name: check_floors
nodes.summary: Compares results against committed score floors and fails the run on regression.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full reproduction: prerequisites, lock, container, datasets, manifest, selected benchmarks, ablations, summary and floor check.

nodes.name: _bench_memories_hnsw
nodes.summary: Creates the _bench_memories_hnsw table (id, heat, 384-dim pgvector embedding), a random unit-vector generator function, seeds rows, and builds the HNSW cosine index used by the UPDATE-cost probe.

nodes.name: _bench_results
nodes.summary: Defines the HNSW UPDATE-cost probe: the _bench_results table and PL/pgSQL helpers for per-row, batched UNNEST, IS-DISTINCT-FROM-gated and per-row-commit heat updates, plus heat reset, comparing five conditions with three replicates each.

nodes.name: phase1_b_e
nodes.summary: Phase 1 of the HNSW probe: with the HNSW index present, runs conditions B (batched UNNEST UPDATE) and E (batched + IS DISTINCT FROM gating) with warmup and three replicates, recording timings into _bench_results.

nodes.name: phase2_c_d
nodes.summary: Phase 2 of the HNSW probe: drops the HNSW index, vacuums, and runs control conditions C (per-row) and D (batched) to isolate the index maintenance cost of heat UPDATEs.

nodes.name: phase3_a
nodes.summary: Phase 3 of the HNSW probe: rebuilds the HNSW index (m=16, ef_construction=64), reports its size, and runs condition A (per-row UPDATE with HNSW) for three replicates.

nodes.name: probe_a
nodes.summary: Quick directional probe: one warmup and one measurement of condition A (HNSW present, per-row UPDATE) to gauge cost before the full run.

nodes.name: bench_container.sh

nodes.name: bench_only.sh

nodes.name: bench_regression.sh
nodes.summary: Shell library implementing the no-regression gate: runs LongMemEval and LoCoMo at a baseline git ref in a temporary worktree against the same container, then compares scores to HEAD within a tolerance (default 0.005).

nodes.name: n_scan_templates.txt

nodes.name: wait_for_db

nodes.name: start_db
nodes.summary: Starts the ephemeral pgvector container on an explicit or docker-assigned port, sets BENCH_DB_URL and waits for readiness.

nodes.name: bench_only_canonical_token
nodes.summary: Maps a benchmark selection token or alias (e.g. longmemeval-s, beam-100K) to its canonical name, failing for unknown tokens.

nodes.name: validate_only
nodes.summary: Rewrites the ONLY variable into canonical comma-separated tokens or fails with exit 2 and the accepted list on empty or unknown tokens.

nodes.name: preflight_regression_datasets
nodes.summary: Checks that the HEAD datasets needed by the selected regression benchmarks exist before running the baseline.

nodes.name: copy_regression_datasets
nodes.summary: Copies the HEAD benchmark datasets into the baseline worktree so both runs use identical data.

nodes.name: run_baseline_benchmarks
nodes.summary: Creates a detached worktree at BASELINE_REF, runs LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo there against the shared container, and cleans up the worktree.

nodes.name: check_regression
nodes.summary: Runs an inline Python comparison of HEAD vs baseline result JSONs and fails if any metric drops beyond REGRESSION_TOLERANCE.

nodes.name: 001-zero-dependencies.md
nodes.summary: ADR-001 records the original Node.js-era decision to ship with zero external npm dependencies, relying only on built-in modules to avoid supply-chain risk and host conflicts.

nodes.name: 002-clean-architecture-layers.md
nodes.summary: ADR-002 adopts Clean Architecture concentric layers (shared, core, infrastructure, handlers, server) with inward-only dependency rules, replacing the original monolithic index.js.

nodes.name: 003-felder-silverman-model.md
nodes.summary: ADR-003 selects the Felder-Silverman learning-style dimensions (active/reflective, sensing/intuitive, sequential/global) plus categorical classifiers for cognitive profiling from session behavior.

nodes.name: 004-jaccard-over-cosine-similarity.md
nodes.summary: ADR-004 chooses Jaccard set similarity over cosine similarity for small keyword-set comparisons in entry-point classification and domain clustering.

nodes.name: 005-agglomerative-over-kmeans-clustering.md
nodes.summary: ADR-005 chooses threshold-based agglomerative clustering (Jaccard, 0.3 merge threshold) over k-means for grouping session first messages into entry-point patterns.

nodes.name: 006-ema-for-incremental-updates.md
nodes.summary: ADR-006 adopts an exponential moving average (alpha 0.1) with probabilistic adoption for categorical dimensions to incrementally update cognitive style after each session.

nodes.name: 007-head-tail-jsonl-reading.md
nodes.summary: ADR-007 decides to read only the first 32KB and last 8KB of conversation JSONL files, bounding I/O per session while capturing entry points and outcomes.

nodes.name: 008-handler-as-composition-root.md
nodes.summary: ADR-008 establishes handlers as composition roots that wire infrastructure I/O into pure core functions and format responses, keeping core side-effect free.

nodes.name: 009-node-test-over-jest.md
nodes.summary: ADR-009 records the legacy choice of the built-in node:test runner over Jest, consistent with the zero-dependency principle of ADR-001.

nodes.name: 010-sparse-dictionary-learning.md
nodes.summary: ADR-010 adopts greedy K-SVD dictionary learning with OMP sparse coding over a 27-dimensional behavioral activation space, with a seed dictionary for cold start.

nodes.name: 011-persona-vector-design.md
nodes.summary: ADR-011 extends the Felder-Silverman cognitive style into a multi-dimensional persona vector used for persona comparison, drift detection and context steering.

nodes.name: 012-python-migration.md
nodes.summary: ADR-012 documents the 12-phase bottom-up migration of the Methodology Agent from zero-dependency Node.js to Python while preserving the Clean Architecture layers.

nodes.name: 013-zikkaron-thermodynamic-memory.md
nodes.summary: ADR-013 introduces the thermodynamic memory model: predictive-coding write gate, heat/decay, intent-aware retrieval and automatic consolidation for persistent cross-session memory.

nodes.name: ADR-0044-upstream-mcp-ingest.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0044 replaces the removed run_pipeline orchestration with Cortex acting as a consumer that ingests artefacts from upstream MCP servers (automatised-pipeline, prd-spec-generator).

nodes.name: ADR-0045-scalability-governance-rules.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0045 codifies scalability governance rules R1-R7 (no SELECT *, streaming ingestion, no full-graph materialization, no raw heat writes, latency classes, measured speedup claims) from a multi-agent audit of a 66K-memory store.

nodes.name: ADR-0046-automatised-pipeline-integration.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0046 proposes integrating the Rust automatised-pipeline code property graph into Cortex's workflow graph so file nodes gain internal symbol structure via the ap_bridge.

nodes.name: ADR-0047-entity-positioning-gap10.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0047 sets radial-slot and force-simulation positioning constants for entity nodes added to the workflow graph visualization (Gap 10 follow-up).

nodes.name: ADR-0048-zetetic-memory-bridge.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0048 bridges the Zetetic agent memory_scope tags into Cortex agent_context/agent_topic so replicated agent memories are scoped and surfaced in agent briefings.

nodes.name: ADR-0049-cortex-stays-local-managed-agents-migration.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0049 keeps Cortex local on main and defers a server-side Managed Agents migration to a feature branch after a readiness audit of the memory_20250818 contract layers.

nodes.name: ADR-0050-marketplace-only-no-uvx.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0050 makes the plugin marketplace the only supported install path, removing the uvx/PyPI launch mode after repeated oscillation between launch commands.

nodes.name: ADR-0051-wiki-page-sources-schema.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0051 adds a dual schema surface for persisting wiki page-to-source-file linkage so documented source paths reach the database and downstream cortex-viz.

nodes.name: ADR-0052-ap-cortex-ingestion-direction-and-precedence.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0052 fixes the automatised-pipeline to Cortex data-flow direction, ingestion precedence rules, and the ap_bridge contract boundary.

nodes.name: ADR-0053-deliberate-reheat-cas-writer-i2-exception.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0053 grants a bounded exception to the I2 canonical-writer invariant for a compare-and-swap deliberate memory re-heat writer.

nodes.name: ADR-0054-spread-activation-domain-scoping.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0054 domain-scopes the spread_activation_memories recall channel so entity-graph spreading activation no longer leaks memories across domains, with benchmark evidence.

nodes.name: ADR-0055-sqlite-connection-per-execution-thread.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0055 proposes request-scoped SQLite connections with thread ownership to stop concurrent MCP handlers from sharing one implicit transaction, comparing four options.

nodes.name: ADR-0056-wiki-decisions-and-reviewable-mirrors.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0056 makes wiki decision pages canonical with generated, reviewable docs mirrors and specifies the governed wiki-write and publication file-safety contracts.

nodes.name: ADR-0057-regulated-write-classes.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0057 records the rationale, extracted from the homeostatic consolidation handler, for regulating automatic writes without suppressing deliberate evidence.

nodes.name: ADR-0058-reversible-extinction.md
nodes.summary: ADR-0058 records the rationale, extracted from active_forgetting, for retaining reversible extinction as an alternative to permanent erasure of memories.

nodes.name: ADR-0059-benchmarks-lib-init-py.md

nodes.name: ADR-0062-benchmarks-lib-xb-drivers-py.md

nodes.name: ADR-0065-benchmarks-lib-bench-container-sh.md

nodes.name: ADR-0066-benchmarks-lib-bench-db-py.md

nodes.name: ADR-0067-benchmarks-lib-bench-regression-sh.md

nodes.name: ADR-0068-benchmarks-lib-blend-weight-sweep-py.md

nodes.name: ADR-0069-benchmarks-lib-capture-origin-mix-py.md

nodes.name: ADR-0070-benchmarks-lib-cross-benchmark-runner-py.md
nodes.summary: Migration ADR preserving decisions in benchmarks/lib/cross_benchmark_runner.py, the pre-registered cross-benchmark generalization test from LongMemEval-S to LoCoMo.

nodes.name: ADR-0071-benchmarks-lib-db-setup-py.md
nodes.summary: Migration ADR preserving decisions in benchmarks/lib/db_setup.py, the deterministic Postgres session GUC setup for reproducible benchmark runs.

nodes.name: ADR-0072-benchmarks-lib-db-snapshot-py.md
nodes.summary: Records the implementation decisions of benchmarks/lib/db_snapshot.py: Postgres pg_dump/restore snapshots with fingerprinting and version-drift enforcement that collapse HNSW build non-determinism.

nodes.name: ADR-0073-benchmarks-lib-decay-sweep-runner-py.md

nodes.name: ADR-0074-benchmarks-lib-disk-space-snapshot-py.md

nodes.name: ADR-0075-benchmarks-lib-e2-subsample-runner-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/e2_subsample_runner.py, the claim-bearing E2 retrieval runner that deterministically subsamples LongMemEval, LoCoMo and BEAM corpora at increasing N.

nodes.name: ADR-0076-benchmarks-lib-e2-zipf-runner-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/e2_zipf_runner.py, which extends E2 past N=1M with a synthetic clustered corpus and Zipfian access events driven through the production read path.

nodes.name: ADR-0077-benchmarks-lib-fusion-py.md
nodes.summary: Short ADR preserving the sourced quality-zone chunk-count bands (Liu et al. 2024) used by benchmarks/lib/fusion.py.

nodes.name: ADR-0078-benchmarks-lib-latency-runner-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/latency_runner.py, a latency-only synthetic-corpus harness measuring per-query wall time and RSS across N, explaining why its retrieval scores are not claim-bearing.

nodes.name: ADR-0079-benchmarks-lib-longitudinal-runner-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/longitudinal_runner.py, a drip-feed harness that spreads synthetic memories over 365 days and probes old vs recent facts to measure decay-aware recall.

nodes.name: ADR-0080-benchmarks-lib-machine-load-snapshot-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/machine_load_snapshot.py, which records host load per benchmark cell after contention silently degraded a trust-factor sweep.

nodes.name: ADR-0081-benchmarks-lib-n-scan-runner-py.md
nodes.summary: Documents that benchmarks/lib/n_scan_runner.py is a deprecated stub superseded by latency_runner, with claim-bearing E2 retrieval moved to the subsample and Zipf runners.

nodes.name: ADR-0082-benchmarks-lib-noise-floor-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/noise_floor.py, which reruns identical configs from one snapshot to measure per-metric variance as the smallest detectable effect threshold.

nodes.name: ADR-0083-benchmarks-lib-numeric-equivalence-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/numeric_equivalence.py, replacing bitwise-exact float identity with tolerance-based equivalence for reordered float32 embedding and scoring work.

nodes.name: ADR-0085-benchmarks-lib-retriever-py.md
nodes.summary: Records the decision in benchmarks/lib/retriever.py to lazy-load FlashRank with the durable production cache_dir instead of /tmp, plus non-silent failure logging.

nodes.name: ADR-0086-benchmarks-lib-run-e1-v3-lme-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/run_e1_v3_lme.py, the serial LongMemEval-S per-mechanism ablation runner (baseline plus 16 mechanisms) emitting summary.csv and manifest.json.

nodes.name: ADR-0087-benchmarks-lib-run-e1-v3-locomo-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/run_e1_v3_locomo.py, the serial two-baseline LoCoMo per-mechanism ablation runner against a shared Postgres instance.

nodes.name: ADR-0088-benchmarks-lib-sweep-progress-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/sweep_progress.py, per-cell checkpoint/resume state for the trust-factor sweep after repeated campaign deaths traced to sub-agent turn termination.

nodes.name: ADR-0089-benchmarks-lib-trust-factor-sweep-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/trust_factor_sweep.py, the cheap adversarial arm of the trust-factor calibration measuring defense across four adversarial scenarios.

nodes.name: ADR-0090-benchmarks-lib-verification-report-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/verification_report.py, the master aggregator that merges JSON results of six verification experiments into a Markdown report for the paper's Limitations section.

nodes.name: ADR-0091-benchmarks-lib-write-manifest-py.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for benchmarks/lib/write_manifest.py, which writes the run MANIFEST.json, extracted verbatim from reproduce.sh to keep provenance logic testable Python.

nodes.name: ADR-0093-mcp-server---main--.md
nodes.summary: Records decisions for mcp_server/__main__.py, the MCP entry point built on the mcp 2.0 SDK's native MCPServer that bridges async handlers as tools after migrating off fastmcp.

nodes.name: ADR-0095-mcp-server-core-ablation.md
nodes.summary: Records the design of mcp_server/core/ablation.py, a lesion-study framework that disables individual neuroscience mechanisms to measure their system-level contribution.

nodes.name: ADR-0096-mcp-server-core-ablation-report.md
nodes.summary: Short ADR preserving the pre-existing interpretation thresholds of mcp_server/core/ablation_report.py, mirrored from ablation.generate_interpretation.

nodes.name: ADR-0097-mcp-server-core-abstention-gate.md

nodes.name: ADR-1068-a-wiki-draft-refinement-must-carry-content.md

nodes.name: ADR-1069-an-empty-value-is-not-a-wiki-draft-refinement.md

nodes.name: ADR-1070-a-draft-section-carries-a-heading-and-a-body-both-text.md

nodes.name: ADR-1071-one-reading-of-a-draft-section-for-every-consumer.md

nodes.name: ADR-1073-reading-a-transcript-has-one-implementation-and-refuses-a-non-path.md

nodes.name: ADR-1076-a-prediction-is-written-open-and-resolved-against-evidence-the-caller-supplies.md

nodes.name: ADR-1077-the-advertised-tool-count-is-read-from-the-registries.md

nodes.name: ADR-1079-report-out-of-convention-git-worktrees-as-an-optional-doctor-warn.md

nodes.name: 0001-zero-dependencies.md
nodes.summary: ADR-001 recording the original Node.js plugin's decision to use zero external npm dependencies, relying only on built-in modules to minimize supply-chain risk and startup cost.

nodes.name: 0002-clean-architecture-layers.md
nodes.summary: ADR-002 adopting six concentric Clean Architecture layers (shared, core, infrastructure, handlers, server, transport) with inward-only dependency rules to replace the monolithic index.js.

nodes.name: 0003-felder-silverman-model.md
nodes.summary: ADR-003 choosing Felder-Silverman learning-style dimensions (active/reflective, sensing/intuitive, sequential/global) plus categorical classifiers for cognitive profiling from session behavior.

nodes.name: 0004-jaccard-over-cosine-similarity.md
nodes.summary: ADR-004 selecting Jaccard set similarity over cosine for comparing small keyword sets between sessions, trading term-frequency sensitivity for simplicity.

nodes.name: 0005-agglomerative-over-kmeans-clustering.md
nodes.summary: ADR-005 choosing agglomerative clustering with a 0.3 Jaccard merge threshold over k-means to cluster session first messages into entry-point patterns without fixing k.

nodes.name: 0006-ema-for-incremental-updates.md
nodes.summary: ADR-006 using an exponential moving average (alpha=0.1) for numeric cognitive-style dimensions and probabilistic adoption for categorical ones to update profiles incrementally per session.

nodes.name: 0007-head-tail-jsonl-reading.md
nodes.summary: ADR-007 bounding conversation JSONL parsing to the first 32KB and last 8KB of each file, trading mid-session visibility for predictable I/O.

nodes.name: 0008-handler-as-composition-root.md
nodes.summary: ADR-008 making each handler a composition root that reads from infrastructure, calls pure core functions and formats the response, keeping core free of I/O.

nodes.name: 0009-node-test-over-jest.md
nodes.summary: ADR-009 choosing the built-in node:test runner over Jest to stay consistent with the zero-dependency principle of the original Node.js implementation.

nodes.name: 0010-sparse-dictionary-learning.md
nodes.summary: ADR-010 adopting greedy K-SVD dictionary learning with OMP sparse coding on a 27-dimensional behavioral activation space to extract interpretable behavioral features, with a seed dictionary for cold start.

nodes.name: 0011-persona-vector-design.md
nodes.summary: ADR-011 extending CognitiveStyle into a multi-dimensional persona vector (thoroughness, autonomy, verbosity, risk tolerance, etc.) for drift detection and context steering.

nodes.name: 0012-python-migration.md

nodes.name: 0013-zikkaron-thermodynamic-memory.md

nodes.name: 0044-upstream-mcp-ingest.md

nodes.name: 0045-scalability-governance-rules.md

nodes.name: 0046-automatised-pipeline-integration.md

nodes.name: 0047-entity-positioning-gap10.md

nodes.name: 0048-zetetic-memory-bridge.md

nodes.name: 0049-cortex-stays-local-managed-agents-migration.md

nodes.name: 0050-marketplace-only-no-uvx.md

nodes.name: 0051-wiki-page-sources-schema.md

nodes.name: test_without_user_site_drops_an_unnormalized_spelling
nodes.summary: The same directory reaches sys.path spelled differently than `site` reports it — a trailing separator, or a `.` segment. Comparing raw strings would keep it, and keeping it is what breaks the import.

nodes.name: test_without_user_site_drops_directories_under_user_site
nodes.summary: `site` processes user site-packages' own .pth files at interpreter start, so a pywin32 installed there has already appended its win32 and win32/lib subdirectories. Leaving those behind keeps exactly the packages this cut exists to displace.

nodes.name: test_user_site_dir_never_raises
nodes.summary: A launch must survive a sysconfig that cannot resolve the user base — and must say so. Returning None leaves user site-packages on sys.path, which is issue #621's symptom exactly, so swallowing the cause would make the bug recur with no trace at all.

nodes.name: test_user_site_dir_stays_quiet_when_it_resolves
nodes.summary: Every hook launch calls this; a diagnostic on the normal path would be noise in eleven hooks' stderr.

nodes.name: ADR-001: Zero External Dependencies
nodes.summary: Use zero external npm dependencies.

nodes.name: ADR-002: Clean Architecture Concentric Layers
nodes.summary: Adopt six concentric layers with strict dependency rules — inner layers never import outer: 1.

nodes.name: ADR-003: Felder-Silverman Model for Cognitive Profiling
nodes.summary: Use Felder-Silverman learning style dimensions: - **Active/Reflective** — Does the developer try things immediately or plan first?

nodes.name: ADR-004: Jaccard Similarity Over Cosine Similarity
nodes.summary: Use Jaccard similarity (`|A∩B| / |A∪B|`) instead of cosine similarity for keyword-level comparisons.

nodes.name: ADR-005: Agglomerative Clustering Over K-Means
nodes.summary: Use agglomerative (hierarchical) clustering with Jaccard similarity and a merge threshold of 0.3.

nodes.name: ADR-006: Exponential Moving Average for Incremental Updates
nodes.summary: Use Exponential Moving Average (EMA) with α=0.1 for numeric dimensions: new_value = α × observed + (1 - α) × previous For categorical dimensions (e.g., debugging style), use probabilistic adoption: the new value is adopted with probability α, otherwise the previous value is retained.

nodes.name: ADR-007: Head+Tail JSONL Reading Strategy
nodes.summary: Read only the first 32KB (head) and last 8KB (tail) of each JSONL file.

nodes.name: ADR-008: Handlers as Composition Roots
nodes.summary: Each handler file serves as a composition root: it reads from infrastructure, passes data to core functions, and formats the response.

nodes.name: ADR-009: node:test Over Jest
nodes.summary: Use Node.js built-in test runner (`node:test` module + `node:assert`) available since Node.js 18.

nodes.name: ADR-010: Sparse Dictionary Learning for Behavioral Features
nodes.summary: Use greedy dictionary learning (simplified K-SVD) with Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) sparse coding on a 27-dimensional behavioral activation space.

nodes.name: ADR-011: 12-Dimensional Persona Vector Design
nodes.summary: Extend CognitiveStyle with 6 additional numeric dimensions derived from behavioral signals, yielding a 9-numeric-dimensional persona vector: 1.

nodes.name: ADR-012: Python Migration from Node.js
nodes.summary: Incrementally port the entire codebase from JavaScript to Python, following a 12-phase bottom-up migration strategy that preserves the Clean Architecture layer structure.

nodes.name: ADR-013: Thermodynamic Memory Model
nodes.summary: Implement a thermodynamic memory architecture in three tiers, each building on the previous: ### Tier 1 -- Core Memory (Predictive Coding + Write Gate) - **Hierarchical predictive coding gate** (`hierarchical_predictive_coding.py`): 3-level Friston free energy gate (sensory/entity/schema) with preci

nodes.name: ADR-0044 — Upstream MCP ingestion (Cortex is the consumer)
nodes.summary: Cortex is the **consumer** of these upstream MCP servers, not the driver.

nodes.name: ADR-0045: Scalability Governance Rules (R1–R6)
nodes.summary: Adopt six governance rules that apply to every change merged to `main`.

nodes.name: ADR-0046: Integration with the `automatised-pipeline` plugin
nodes.summary: Consume `automatised-pipeline` as a sibling MCP server.

nodes.name: ADR-0047 — Entity-node positioning constants (Gap 10 follow-up)
nodes.summary: Give each visible entity a deterministic slot derived from its edges, gated by heat, with two physics-decay constants adjusted for the new N.

nodes.name: ADR-0048: Zetetic memory_scope → Cortex agent_context bridge
nodes.summary: ### 1. Drainer sets `agent_topic` (zetetic-team-subagents) `commands/session/memory-sync.md` now instructs the agent to pass `agent_topic: <scope>` (the job's `scope` field) on every `cortex:remember` call, in addition to the existing `tags`.

nodes.name: ADR-0049 — Cortex stays local on main; server-side Cortex deferred to `feat/server-side-cortex`
nodes.summary: **Cortex stays local on `main`.** No public deployment.

nodes.name: ADR-0050: Marketplace Is the Only Supported Install Path — uvx Removed
nodes.summary: **The plugin marketplace is the only supported Cortex install path.** uvx is **not** removed because it is bad — it is removed because it is **not Anthropic's official mechanism for plugin distribution**.

nodes.name: ADR-0051: Wiki Page-Source Linkage — Dual Schema Surface
nodes.summary: **Dual schema surface**, added to `WIKI_SCHEMA_DDL` and `MIGRATIONS_DDL` in `mcp_server/infrastructure/pg_schema.py`: 1.

nodes.name: ADR-0052: AP↔Cortex Flow Direction, Ingestion Precedence, and the ap_bridge Contract
nodes.summary: ### 1. Flow direction: Cortex pulls, AP never pushes (D1) Every mechanism added in Incrément 5 is a **Cortex-side consumer** of AP's file artifacts — reached via the existing `APBridge` (ADR-0046) or by reading `runs/<run_id>/` directly off disk.

nodes.summary: Applies Cortex's PostgreSQL schema (``pg_schema.get_all_ddl()``) via the exact same hash-gated, advisory-lock-serialized path ``PgMemoryStore._init_schema`` runs at construction — this module never re-derives the DDL set or the migration algorithm, it only decides *whether a migration happened* so i

nodes.name: ADR-0639 — mcp_server/observability/metrics.py rationale
nodes.summary: We emit the text-exposition format (Prometheus 0.0.4 spec) directly.

nodes.name: ADR-0640 — mcp_server/observability/silent_failure.py rationale
nodes.summary: Context (audit 2026-07-11, docs/audits/silent-except-audit-2026-07-11.md): Two production incidents in one night were both the same shape — a broad ``except Exception`` guarding a component that has a real, intentional fallback (skip re-ranking, skip a graph expansion) caught a bug in the *mechanism

nodes.name: ADR-0643 — mcp_server/shared/algorithmic_embedding.py rationale
nodes.summary: The zero-model fallback for ``EmbeddingEngine``: when sentence-transformers is unavailable (import fails, or the model weights are absent and cannot be downloaded), this module produces a fixed-dimension dense vector for any text with no network, no model files, and no learned parameters — only arithmetic seeded by the token strings themselves.

nodes.name: ADR-0644 — mcp_server/shared/categorizer.py rationale
nodes.summary: Returns the highest-scoring category, with tie-breaking favoring multi-word phrase matches.

nodes.name: ADR-0645 — mcp_server/shared/code_tokenize.py rationale
nodes.summary: Cortex memories frequently carry code identifiers — ``normalizePaymentAmount``, ``snake_case_id``, ``HTTPRequest``.

nodes.name: ADR-0646 — mcp_server/shared/content_hardening.py rationale
nodes.summary: Applied at every user-input boundary (remember, ingest_*, backfill) to prevent three classes of defect:

nodes.name: ADR-0647 — mcp_server/shared/domain_mapping.py rationale
nodes.summary: Builds the mapping dynamically from git repos discovered on the filesystem.

nodes.name: ADR-0648 — mcp_server/shared/entity_canonical.py rationale
nodes.summary: Source: Curie I4 completeness audit (2026-04-16) found **111 case-variant duplicate entity groups** on the cortex DB (`Output`/`OUTPUT`, `String`/`STRING`, `DOMAIN`/`domain`, `FilePath`/`filepath`, etc.) across 196 entity rows.

nodes.name: ADR-0649 — mcp_server/shared/freshness.py rationale
nodes.summary: Freshness annotation for injected memories (fleet-watch #110).

nodes.name: ADR-0651 — mcp_server/shared/hook_state_paths.py rationale
nodes.summary: Keep explicit Claude roots independent from legacy global hook state.

nodes.name: ADR-0652 — mcp_server/shared/json_native.py rationale
nodes.summary: Why this exists --------------- The MCP SDK builds a tool's ``structuredContent`` by JSON-serializing the handler's return value and validating it against the declared ``output_schema``.

nodes.name: ADR-0654 — mcp_server/shared/log_file_lock.py rationale
nodes.summary: FileHandler locks are thread-local, not interprocess (Python Logging Cookbook, https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging-cookbook.html).

nodes.name: ADR-0655 — mcp_server/shared/log_rotation.py rationale
nodes.summary: Retain the active file plus one previous segment (.1), the minimum rotating history in Python's RotatingFileHandler contract.

nodes.name: ADR-0658 — mcp_server/shared/minhash.py rationale
nodes.summary: Used by the entity-graph fuzzy deduplicator (``core.entity_dedup``) to block candidate near-duplicate entity labels in sub-quadratic time before the exact Jaro-Winkler verification pass.

nodes.name: ADR-0659 — mcp_server/shared/near_dup_calibration.py rationale
nodes.summary: Calibrate the near-duplicate similarity threshold on measured data (I6-D2, INC6.4 campaign) and group candidate pairs into connected components for supersession.

nodes.name: ADR-0660 — mcp_server/shared/platform.py rationale
nodes.summary: Centralizes the three portability hazards that silently broke Cortex on Windows (each previously open-coded at several call sites):

nodes.name: ADR-0661 — mcp_server/shared/progress.py rationale
nodes.summary: All methods are synchronous.

nodes.name: ADR-0662 — mcp_server/shared/project_ids.py rationale
nodes.summary: Claude Code stores project data in directories named by mangled filesystem paths.

nodes.name: ADR-0663 — mcp_server/shared/redaction.py rationale
nodes.summary: Stdlib only — no project-layer imports.

nodes.name: ADR-0666 — mcp_server/shared/string_distance.py rationale
nodes.summary: Used by the entity-graph fuzzy deduplicator (``core.entity_dedup``) to verify MinHash/LSH candidate pairs.

nodes.name: ADR-0667 — mcp_server/shared/subprocess_safe.py rationale
nodes.summary: Kill-without-recollect subprocess execution — the shared #94 fix.

nodes.name: ADR-0668 — mcp_server/shared/telemetry_context.py rationale
nodes.summary: ContextVar scopes measurements to the current async task/thread.

nodes.name: ADR-0669 — mcp_server/shared/temporal.py rationale
nodes.summary: Deliberately naive (noqa DTZ001 x3 below): every caller (parse_date, compute_date_distance_score) only ever diffs two datetimes produced by THIS module's own date-only parsing — no time-of-day, no tzinfo, on either side of the subtraction.

nodes.name: ADR-0670 — mcp_server/shared/temporal_normalize.py rationale
nodes.summary: Separate from `temporal.py`, which scores dates for retrieval: the two have different reasons to change.

nodes.name: ADR-0671 — mcp_server/shared/temporal_timezones.py rationale
nodes.summary: `dateutil.parser.parse` drops a timezone abbreviation it cannot resolve and returns a *naive* datetime.

nodes.name: ADR-0672 — mcp_server/shared/text.py rationale
nodes.summary: # source: two-tier filter documented in extract_keywords docstring — # tokens >6 chars pass unconditionally, 2-6 char tokens only if technical

nodes.name: ADR-0673 — mcp_server/shared/types_features.py rationale
nodes.summary: Types the internal core-layer boundary between mcp_server/core/{persona_vector, attribution_tracer, behavioral_crosscoder, sparse_dictionary}.py and their consumers (mcp_server/handlers/explore_features.py, mcp_server/core/profile_assembler.py).

nodes.name: ADR-0675 — mcp_server/shared/vader.py rationale
nodes.summary: Minimal VADER sentiment analysis for engineering text.

nodes.name: ADR-0676 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_classification.py rationale
nodes.summary: Implements the schema from ADR-2244 (richer wiki classification).

nodes.name: ADR-0677 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_decision_ids.py rationale
nodes.summary: Canonical decision identity (issue #514, ADR-0056), independent of storage.

nodes.name: ADR-0678 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_frontmatter.py rationale
nodes.summary: Parses YAML-style frontmatter (``---``…``---``) into a plain dict so handlers can round-trip metadata without depending on a YAML library, and renders a ``PageDocument`` back to markdown text.

nodes.name: ADR-0679 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_frontmatter_validation.py rationale
nodes.summary: Closes the corruption class that PR #104 (commit 53712df8) repaired reactively at read-time inside ``wiki_pages.parse_page`` (dup-label strip, quote strip).

nodes.name: ADR-0680 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_index.py rationale
nodes.summary: # source: structural — a wiki path is kind/filename (2 parts) or # kind/domain/filename (3 parts); see the build_index docstring below.

nodes.name: ADR-0681 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_ir.py rationale
nodes.summary: Each IR is a named, inspectable boundary between pipeline phases:

nodes.name: ADR-0682 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_layout.py rationale
nodes.summary: The wiki is an authored long-form Markdown layer.

nodes.name: ADR-0683 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_page_builders.py rationale
nodes.summary: Render a spec / PRD / design doc page.

nodes.name: ADR-0684 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_pages.py rationale
nodes.summary: Design intent: pages are *authored* content, not derived views.

nodes.name: ADR-0685 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_readme.py rationale
nodes.summary: The wiki's technical content lives in `<kind>/<domain>/<slug>.md` files with templated front-matter + section structure — tech-ready, but dense.

nodes.name: ADR-0686 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_schema_loader.py rationale
nodes.summary: The wiki describes its own schema.

nodes.name: ADR-0687 — mcp_server/shared/wiki_source_paths.py rationale
nodes.summary: Canonical form for wiki page -> source-file path linkage (ADR-0051 STEP 2).

nodes.name: ADR-0688 — mcp_server/shared/write_class.py rationale
nodes.summary: Design doc: ``scratchpad/memoire-qui-comprend-design.md`` §M-D2 (taxonomy table) + §M-D3 (homeostatic stratification, this module's first consumer).

nodes.name: ADR-0690 — mcp_server/telemetry_middleware.py rationale
nodes.summary: The SDK converts handler exceptions to TextContent inside call_next.

nodes.name: ADR-0691 — mcp_server/tool_error_handler.py rationale
nodes.summary: Wraps handler exceptions so users never see raw Python tracebacks.

nodes.name: ADR-0692 — mcp_server/tool_profile_middleware.py rationale
nodes.summary: MCP-SDK middleware enforcing the active tool profile (issue #177).

nodes.name: ADR-0693 — mcp_server/tool_profiles.py rationale
nodes.summary: Cortex registers its whole tool surface to every client on every session (issue #177): the largest fixed token cost in the ecosystem, paid before the user types anything.

nodes.name: ADR-0696 — mcp_server/tool_registry_ingest.py rationale
nodes.summary: ingest_codebase — pulls from ai-architect-mcp-codebase MCP change_impact — pulls from ai-architect-mcp-codebase MCP (ADR-0046) ingest_prd — pulls from prd-spec-generator MCP ingest_findings — reads AP findings artifacts directly off disk (INC5.1) ingest_document — reads .docx / Confluence export fil

nodes.name: ADR-0698 — mcp_server/tool_registry_memory.py rationale
nodes.summary: Import conversation history into the memory store.

nodes.name: ADR-0700 — mcp_server/tool_registry_wiki.py rationale
nodes.summary: Registers the authoring surface that lets Claude maintain a first-class Markdown wiki (ADRs, specs, file docs, notes) alongside PostgreSQL memory.

layers.name: MCP Server Entry & Tool Registry
layers.description: FastMCP entry point (__main__), tool_registry_* modules registering the memory/wiki/navigation tool surface, tool profiles and middleware, migrate CLI, and the doctor preflight checks.

layers.name: Handlers (Composition Roots)
layers.description: Per-tool MCP handlers (remember, recall, consolidate, wiki_*, etc.) that wire pure core logic to infrastructure stores; the only layer importing both core and infrastructure.

layers.name: Core Memory Logic
layers.description: Pure, I/O-free business logic: thermodynamic heat/decay, predictive-coding write gates, consolidation cascade, retrieval fusion, cognitive profiling, streaming and context assembly.

layers.name: Infrastructure (Storage & I/O)
layers.description: All I/O adapters: PostgreSQL+pgvector and SQLite stores, schema/migrations, embedding engine, scanners over ~/.claude, artifact store, MCP client pool and config.

layers.name: Shared Kernel & Cross-Cutting
layers.description: Stdlib-only shared utilities and Pydantic types plus cross-cutting observability/telemetry, error hierarchy and per-tool argument validation used by every layer.

layers.name: Session Lifecycle Hooks
layers.description: Claude Code/Codex hook entry points (SessionStart, PostToolUse auto-capture, compaction checkpoint, SessionEnd) that inject and capture memories around agent sessions.

layers.name: Test Suites & Fuzzing
layers.description: pytest suites mirroring each mcp_server layer plus scripts/benchmarks/invariants/architecture tests, JS host tests, and atheris fuzz harnesses with corpora.

layers.name: Benchmarks & Results
layers.description: LongMemEval/LoCoMo/BEAM and mechanism benchmarks, shared bench lib, HNSW/pg recall probes, and committed result JSON/CSV artifacts that source the zetetic constants.

layers.name: Build, Deploy & Distribution
layers.description: Project configs (pyproject, package.json, pyright, craftsmanship/zetetic gates), maintenance and launcher scripts with SQL migrations, Docker/devcontainer, GitHub Actions CI, and plugin/marketplace packaging (plugins, skills, slash commands, manifests).

layers.name: Documentation, ADRs & Wiki
layers.description: Root project docs (README, PRIVACY, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING), docs/ ADRs, provenance audits, campaigns, arXiv papers, and the wiki/adr knowledge pages.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Cortex (published as hypermnesia-mcp) is a local-first persistent memory MCP server for AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex. The README covers how memories are admitted, verified, corrected and decayed, along with the retrieval benchmark evidence, the storage backends and the host integrations. PRIVACY.md says where data lives: a local SQLite file by default, or your own PostgreSQL. It also lists the only outbound traffic, which is model downloads and integrations you opt into.

tour.title: Architecture and Ground Rules
tour.description: Before you read any code, learn the layering the project relies on: server -> handlers -> core <- shared, with infrastructure -> shared, and handlers as the only composition roots. The module inventory lists each layer and its dependency-rules table. CLAUDE.md and agent-guidance.md add the non-negotiables: no source, no implementation; benchmark before commit; no silent fallbacks. Every later step fits into one of these layers.

tour.title: Server Entry Point
tour.description: mcp_server/__main__.py is the top code entry point and the root of the dependency BFS. It builds the MCPServer with telemetry and tool-profile middleware, registers every tool registry and prompt, applies schema metadata, and serves over stdio with a signal-driven shutdown. Its direct dependencies include hooks/wiring.py, the single idempotent composition root that connects core's I/O injection seams to their infrastructure implementations. That wiring keeps core pure.
tour.languageLesson: __main__.py makes a package runnable with `python -m mcp_server`. Python runs this module when the package itself is executed, which keeps the CLI entry separate from importable library code.

tour.title: The MCP Tool Surface
tour.description: The server exposes its capabilities as MCP tools. The tool_registry_* modules group them by tier: tool_registry_memory registers remember, recall and unified_search, and tool_registry_core registers the cognitive-profiling tools. _tool_meta.py, one of the most-imported files, derives each tool's registration kwargs and output schemas from the handler schemas. docs/mcp-tools.md lists every tool with its purpose and target latency.
tour.languageLesson: Decorator-based registration (e.g. `@mcp.tool(...)`) attaches metadata to a plain function and records it in a registry when the module is imported. FastMCP uses this to turn typed Python handlers into JSON-schema-described tools.

tour.title: Configuration and Store Selection
tour.description: Each tool needs storage, and memory_store.py is the most-depended-upon file in the graph. It is a runtime-aware factory that picks PostgreSQL or SQLite and caches one shared store per (backend, url, dim) key. memory_config.py defines the MemorySettings Pydantic model, which you can override through CORTEX_MEMORY_ environment variables. This factory is how the two backends described in PRIVACY.md (Step 1) become a single interface.
tour.languageLesson: Pydantic settings models validate configuration at load time and can read values from prefixed environment variables, so a mistyped config value fails at load time instead of causing a silent error later.

tour.title: Storage Backends and Schema
tour.description: The two backends behind the factory are built from mixins. sqlite_store.py composes SQLite, FTS5 and sqlite-vec mixins and runs recall plumbing on the client side. pg_store.py assembles the PostgreSQL + pgvector mixins and a psycopg pool. pg_schema.py holds the full DDL, including the PL/pgSQL recall_memories() and effective_heat() procedures, so on PostgreSQL much of the retrieval fusion runs inside the database.
tour.languageLesson: Mixin composition: a class like `PgMemoryStore(EntitiesMixin, QueriesMixin, ...)` inherits small, focused method sets from several parents. This keeps each file under the project's 300-line craftsmanship limit while presenting one store API.

tour.title: Writing a Memory
tour.description: The remember tool shows the full write path. handlers/remember.py is a composition root: it hardens the arguments, resolves domain and origin, then calls pure core logic. core/write_gate.py scores four novelty signals (embedding, entity, temporal and structural) and applies neuromodulation and other modulations. hierarchical_predictive_coding.py adds a three-level Friston free-energy gate, and thermodynamics.py assigns heat, importance and valence before the memory is inserted.

tour.title: Recalling Memories
tour.description: Retrieval mirrors the write path. handlers/recall.py combines pg_recall's intent-adaptive WRRF fusion with prospective triggers, Hebbian co-activation, neuro-symbolic rules and receipts. query_intent.py classifies a query as temporal, causal, entity and so on, and maps it to signal weights. recall_pipeline.py then applies the post-fusion stages: Hopfield and HDC reranks, spreading activation and reconsolidation. reranker.py adds a FlashRank cross-encoder pass.

tour.title: Consolidation and Decay
tour.description: Memories change after they are stored. The consolidate handler runs decay, compression, complementary-learning-systems (CLS) abstraction and the cascade cycles, and times each cycle. cascade_stages.py defines the stages a memory moves through, from labile to early and late LTP, each with its own decay rate and heat floor. cascade_advancement.py decides when a memory advances. consolidation_engine.py plans the move from episodic to semantic memory, which is the 'forgetting curve' side of the heat introduced in Step 7.

tour.title: Session Lifecycle Hooks
tour.description: Hooks make Cortex automatic, so the agent does not have to call remember and recall explicitly. session_start.py injects anchored and hot memories plus checkpoint state as a context banner. post_tool_capture.py captures significant tool outputs and gists oversized ones into artifacts. session_lifecycle.py updates profiles at SessionEnd. The plugin manifest wires these hooks into Claude Code, and the Codex hooks.json does the same for Codex, which is how both agents share one memory.

tour.title: The Self-Curating Wiki
tour.description: Beyond episodic memories, Cortex keeps a per-project wiki of ADRs, specs and notes. wiki_write.py writes pages atomically and syncs wiki.pages, citations and a protected pointer memory, so recall can reach wiki knowledge. ADR-0056 is the most-referenced document in the graph: it makes wiki decision pages canonical, with reviewable docs mirrors generated from them.

tour.title: Ablation and Benchmarks
tour.description: The zetetic rule from Step 2 needs evidence behind every mechanism. ablation.py, which many files import, is a lesion-study framework: it can switch off any mechanism and measure the impact. benchmarks/reproduce.sh is the release gate. It starts an isolated, ephemeral PostgreSQL container, runs LongMemEval, LoCoMo and BEAM on pinned datasets, and enforces score floors. Runners like longmemeval/run_benchmark.py report MRR and Recall@k, and the Makefile targets delegate to reproduce.sh.

tour.title: Quality Gates and Health Checks
tour.description: Several gates enforce the rules introduced earlier. check_craftsmanship.py flags files over 300 lines, methods over 40 lines, layer-import violations and constants without a source comment, compared against a committed baseline. observability/silent_failure.py puts the 'no silent fallbacks' rule into practice: it records every swallowed failure and exposes a metric for it. doctor.py runs backend-aware preflight checks with a fix hint for each failure.

tour.title: Packaging, CI and Deployment
tour.description: These files package the server and test every change. pyproject.toml defines the console scripts and the optional extras (sqlite, postgresql, otel and others). The multi-stage Dockerfile installs the uv.lock-pinned dependencies in a builder stage and runs `python -m mcp_server` as a non-root user in a slim runtime stage. ci.yml runs the test matrix, the SQLite and Windows legs, ruff, the craftsmanship gate, pyright and a bare-container smoke test on every push.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use several FROM stages. The builder stage carries the compile-time tooling, and only the built wheel and runtime dependencies are copied into the final image, which keeps it small and limits what an attacker could exploit.
